A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PACO and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–H. Their content can be reliably matched despite section reorganization and added comparisons.

before.justification: v1 reports original summarization experiments, value-function ablations, attribute-weight sensitivity results, and runtime measurements in Tables 1–6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluations of two generation-budget-matched comparison methods in Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: PACO retains its summary-level nodes, single-attribute actions, PUCT search, rewards, and final-summary selection procedure. Algorithm 1 and the appendix prompts are unchanged. Heuristic scoring moves into a variants subsection; the newly disclosed decoding settings do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same attributes on MACSumDial, MACSumDoc, and DialogSum, covering meetings, news, and everyday dialogue. The added comparisons use retained datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds Joint-iterative and Random sequential as evaluated 70B comparators on both MACSum datasets (Section 3.2; Tables 1–2). These introduce a substantively stronger comparison class that controls generation effort; all existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: The new comparisons match generation counts to PACO's eight simulations and select the best-controlled candidate (Section 3.2; Appendix B). This adds a focused experimental control. Retained metrics and search limits are unchanged; beam-search settings are newly disclosed rather than explicitly revised.

E4.justification: The added controlled comparisons examine whether gains reflect structured planning rather than additional attempts, and whether sequential adjustment helps relative to joint revision. Existing value-function ablations, control-pattern analyses, and Appendix D's attribute-weight sensitivity study are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-evaluation seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added generation-budget information describes candidate-search effort, not statistical replication or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 add substantive results against the new controls while retaining existing numerical results. On MACSumDial, length MAD is 11.19 for Joint-iterative and 11.16 for Random sequential, versus PACO's unchanged 7.63; on MACSumDoc, the corresponding values are 7.15, 6.62, and 4.81. PACO leads these controls on deterministic attributes, but not topic alignment.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and search equations retain their substance. The displayed heuristic-probability equation becomes an equivalent prose definition in Section 3.3; equation renumbering and leaf-index notation cleanup introduce no new mathematical reasoning or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: training-free adaptive MCTS planning, strong multi-attribute control across models and domains, and preserved summary quality. The added comparisons support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the matched-generation results as evidence for structured planning and sequential refinement (Section 5), and adds a beam-search rationale in Appendix B. It also softens the limitation discussion by removing the explicit limited-scalability warning while retaining computational expense and suggesting approximation strategies.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies beam size 3, temperature 1.0, top_k 50, and top_p 1.0, and documents generation-count matching for the new controls. Hardware, existing search hyperparameters, Algorithm 1, and detailed prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Retkowski and Waibel (2025) and Gu et al. (2025) to the single-attribute control discussion. PACO's research positioning remains stable; publication updates for Lee et al. and Ryu et al. concern already cited works.

P1.justification: v2 presents PACO before the comparison methods, introduces Problem formulation and MCTS design subsections, and groups self-planning and heuristic scoring under Methods Variants. It also revises selected explanations, affiliations, and acknowledgments, while retaining most prose and the broader document structure.

P2.justification: Tables 1–3 group results by backbone, highlight PACO rows, and change bolding to comparisons within each backbone; Tables 1–2 also accommodate the new comparators. Appendix tables receive related formatting changes, and figures undergo sizing or caption adjustments. The existing plots and illustrated findings are retained.

improvement.justification: The equal-generation controls address an important weakness in v1: its comparisons did not isolate structured planning from additional generation attempts. PACO's deterministic-attribute advantage over both new controls on both MACSum datasets substantially strengthens validation of the central contribution. Appendix B also improves reproducibility. Generation matching does not establish equal runtime, and the scalability warning is softened, but these qualifications do not outweigh the stronger empirical support.
